## Audit report: "stockfish" references in `/home/user/lance-graph`

**Bottom line up front:** There is no chess engine, NNUE evaluator, or `stockfish-rs` source tree inside this repository or anywhere on this filesystem. Every reference falls into one of three buckets: (A) one real, built, in-repo Rust example that validates this workspace's own palette/Fisher-z codec against an externally-produced NNUE data file; (B) doc-comment citations/analogies to Stockfish's NNUE architecture as design precedent; (C) plan-doc references to `AdaWorldAPI/stockfish-rs`, described as a real *sibling* repository with its own commits/PRs, but one plan doc explicitly records that this repo's own audit found it **unverifiable in this environment** — it is not checked out, not vendored, and not a Cargo dependency anywhere in `lance-graph`.

---

### 1. `crates/bgz-tensor/examples/nnue_palette_cosine.rs` — BUILT (real code, category A)

Full file read. This is a real, compiling example (`cargo run --manifest-path crates/bgz-tensor/Cargo.toml --release --example nnue_palette_cosine`). Doc header (lines 1–25):

> `//! D-PALETTE-NNUE (corrected) — does the CERTIFIED palette256 cosine-replacement preserve the pairwise-cosine ranking of NNUE feature-transformer columns?`
> `//! Correction of the first cut (`stockfish-rs examples/palette_nnue.rs`), which used a hand-rolled scalar k-means codebook ... wrong tool, wrong methodology. This probe reuses the real codec, `bgz_tensor::fisher_z::FisherZTable` ...`
> `//! Input: the 256 FT columns (1024-dim f32) exported by `stockfish-rs --example export_ft_columns` ...`

What it actually does: it does **not** implement or run NNUE. It reads a binary file of NNUE feature-transformer columns (produced elsewhere, by the external `stockfish-rs` project, path from `$FT_COLUMNS_OUT`/arg1/default `/tmp/ft_columns.bin`), builds a `FisherZTable` (this workspace's own i8 codec), computes true cosine vs. palette-restored cosine over all off-diagonal pairs, and gates GREEN/AMBER/FAIL on Spearman ρ thresholds (`ρ_all ≥ 0.999 && ρ_mid ≥ 0.99`, lines 197–224). If the input file is absent, it prints a message and exits 0 (CI-safe no-op) — line 124–128: `"nnue_palette_cosine: no FT-columns file at {} (run stockfish-rs export_ft_columns first) — skipping."`

Measured GREEN-path output text (lines 198–205): `"D-PALETTE-NNUE (corrected): GREEN — ρ_all {:.5} ≥ 0.999 ... The NNUE FT columns ARE a palette256 tenant: the certified Fisher-z cosine-replacement preserves pairwise-cosine ranking (one-table-read similarity), no materialization."`

So: this is a real, built validator of this workspace's own codec, using NNUE weight data as a demanding test corpus — not an NNUE implementation, and not a chess engine. The NNUE data itself must be supplied from outside this repo (by the external `stockfish-rs` tool); nothing in `lance-graph` generates it.

### 2. `crates/jc/src/reliability.rs` — CITATION only (category B)

Doc comment, lines 1–14, gives the motivation for consolidating Pearson/Spearman/Cronbach/ICC into one module: `"until now each caller rolled its own (e.g. a private `spearman_rho` on rankings in `probe_p1_gamma_phase.rs`, and a hand-rolled `spearman_rho` in the stockfish-rs probe)."` No stockfish code appears in the file; it is purely citing an external repo's duplicate implementation as the reason this crate exists.

### 3. `crates/lance-graph-planner/src/temporal.rs` (line 856) and `crates/lance-graph-contract/src/temporal_pov.rs` (line 37) — CITATION / claimed external consumer (category B/C)

`temporal_pov.rs:37-41`: cross-references `.claude/knowledge/stockfish-nnue-as-perturbation-cascade.md` and describes `D-SF-EPISODIC-1` as "a game as a `temporal.rs`-shaped version-stream ... measured byte-identical GREEN both fresh-from-FEN (34/34 plies) and out-of-order replay (11/11 queries)."

Neither file contains stockfish code. Both describe `TemporalPov`/`VersionRange` as zero-dep types meant to be *consumed by* an external repo (`stockfish-rs`). No stockfish-rs source exists in this filesystem to verify that consumption actually happens.

### 4. `crates/perturbation-sim/COMPUTE_DAG_MAPPING.md` — Analogy (category B)

Lines 44–53: `"Stockfish NNUE is the existence proof that the incremental side works at scale; this crate is the existence proof that the bound holding it together is real."` Pure architectural-precedent framing for `perturbation-sim`'s own Weyl-bound proof; no code, no dependency.

### 5. Plan docs — four read for stockfish content

**`.claude/plans/SYNERGY-MAP-S00-S07.md`** — the most substantive. Treats `stockfish-rs` as a real sibling repo pinned at commit `f3f728a` (header, line 8), cataloguing types allegedly owned there (`GameEpisodeKey` at `episode.rs:92`, `DecisionEpisodeV1` at `episode.rs:171`, `TeacherTrace`, `CandidatePolicy`, etc., lines 60–128) as "SOLID" and reuse-only ("never linked" as a dependency). The claim was unverifiable by construction."` It concludes (lines 321–334) that the *only* measured Stockfish seam is `nnue_palette_cosine.rs` validating the palette codec against an exported data blob — `"NNUE's role here is a demanding dataset that validates a codec, not a mechanism the substrate imitates."`

**`.claude/plans/epistemic-quadrant-materialization-v1.md`** §7-T, "the stockfish-rs baby step (**prepare, not build**)" (line 466): explicitly future/unbuilt. Line 474–479: `"GPL fence (iron): stockfish-rs is GPL-3.0 and NEVER becomes a dependency of lance-graph. The seam is data-only — stockfish-rs emits labeled records (FEN, legal moves, evals, PV) as artifacts; lance-graph consumes records ... **`.claude/plans/temporal-markov-and-style-classes-v1.md`** (lines 45–51): cites a knowledge doc allegedly in the `stockfish-rs` sibling repo about pext/Morton bit-tricks, with an explicit negative finding: `"Stockfish has NO Morton/pyramid/palette/comma code (verified, zero hits); what DOES transfer is the `Magic` struct's `pext`/`pdep` gather→table-lookup→scatter pattern ... as a candidate AVX-512/BMI2 fast path."` Technique-transfer citation, not integration.

`D2.md:33`: table row calling `temporal_pov.rs` `"the surface external consumers (stockfish-rs) use."` `D3.md:102–113`: describes a `temporal.rs` test and states `"The test's own doc comment cross-references `AdaWorldAPI/stockfish-rs examples/hindsight_stream.rs` (`D-SF-HINDSIGHT-1`) as consuming 'the zero-dep `TemporalPov` mirror of this exact machinery' against real lichess games — evidence the abstraction is meant to travel beyond this one repo."` Both are architecture docs describing/citing an external consumer relationship, not code in this repo.

### 7. Is there a real `stockfish-rs` crate/checkout? — No, and no dependency wiring

- `grep -rn "stockfish-rs"` across `.claude`, `docs`, and all `Cargo.toml` files: **zero hits in any `Cargo.toml`.** All hits are in Markdown plan/board/knowledge docs and Rust doc-comments (`//!`, `///`).
- `find /home/user -maxdepth 2 -iname "*stockfish*"`: **zero matches.** The sibling directory list at `/home/user` (`AriGraph, MedCare-rs, OGAR, OGIT, Sharepoint-rs, WoA, burn, deno, home-automation-rs, lance-graph, leptonica, ndarray, openproject-nexgen-rs, openstreetmap-website-rs, q2, ractor, redmine, redmine-rs, rig, rs-graph-llm, ruff, sculpt-3D, shakmaty, tesseract-rs, vart, woa-rs`) contains no `stockfish-rs`, only `shakmaty` (a chess-rules-only crate, cited as what a hypothetical stockfish-rs integration would consume "for rules, never re-implemented").

- The explicit iron rule recorded in the plan docs (`epistemic-quadrant-materialization-v1.md:474`) is that `stockfish-rs` is GPL-3.0 and **"NEVER becomes a dependency of lance-graph"** — any data exchange is file-based (exported columns / labeled records), never a linked crate.
